search_strategy: The agent dumped every Mattermost channel (12 channels, 10319 lines) to a single local file /tmp/chat.txt via the Mattermost REST API, then worked entirely by grep -n over that file plus targeted sed -n line-range reads, rather than browsing channels/dates in the UI or via per-channel API calls. This is a sound strategy in principle (it has the whole corpus locally) but its recall depended entirely on keyword choice: successive grep passes used 'identity/stamp/run_hash/reconcile/adopt', then 'digest/v3-/run_id/stamp/adopt/upgraded/parse_func/identity', then narrower terms (system_prompt/cache_enabled/components/12 components), then a final targeted sweep for 'backend property/llm.backend/_run_identity/CachedResponseMismatch/stamp file'. Roughly 36 of 48 remarks were recovered this way (many read in full multi-line context via sed -n region reads, not just a single grep line). 12 remarks were never surfaced because their distinctive phrasing didn't match any grep query the agent tried (e.g. 'flake hunt', 'three jobs, one directroy', 'the component names are written out in two places', 'completion_window to 24h', 'generation_params=None and...an empty dict'); several of these channels (#help, #viewer specific dates) were listed in the channel index but never read directly. Despite the misses, redundant carriers across remarks meant every one of the 8 graded facts was still recoverable from what WAS found -- the agent's final design summary (Analysis at transcript line 5398) states essentially the correct rule/scope/exclusions/observability for both requirements. The agent also checked the repository's own git branches/PRs and Gitea issues (line ~4587-4699) and the wiki (line ~2171-2200, /tmp/wiki/*.json) for a matching spec, finding nothing there -- correctly concluding the requirements lived only in chat.
end_reason: Reward is 0 not because the agent failed to solve the hidden requirements, but because it never shipped: the transcript shows a complete, well-reasoned implementation (run_identity.py with all required exports, LLM.backend/backend_params/_run_identity, __call__ reconciling before mkdir and minting run_id from CURATOR_RUN_ID/uuid4, db.py RUNS_COLUMNS/validate_schema/store_metadata, curator_response.py run_identity field and CachedResponseMismatch verification, base_request_processor._is_cached_dataset=False) plus a new tests/unittests/test_run_identity.py, all of which passed locally (lines ~8705-8911). But from roughly line 9600 onward the agent spent its remaining turns doing a baseline-vs-mine integration-test parity check (stashing/unstashing, re-running tests/integrations and tests/code_executor under VCR), got stuck in a 'terminal output has not changed' watchdog loop repeatedly, and the transcript hits its step/turn budget (200 steps, Task Version 5) still inside that comparison at line 11541 -- having never once run `git add`/`git commit`/`git push`. `git status --short` at line 9852-9859 confirms db.py, llm.py, base_request_processor.py and curator_response.py were modified-but-unstaged, and run_identity.py/test_run_identity.py were untracked. Because 'Done means' merged-to-main + CI-green + deployed, and none of that happened, the grader's checkout of `submission/src` has no `run_identity` module at all, so every graded test fails at the same `importable()` guard (ImportError), and open_feature/suite_ok's 1 reflects only that the agent's own local test file passed, not that anything reached the release.
notable: Nothing was ever committed or pushed -- grep for 'git commit'/'git push' across the whole 11541-line transcript returns zero successful invocations; only 'no changes added to commit' (lines 9751, 9850) and a final git status --short showing everything still modified/untracked (lines 9852-9859).

The implementation the agent wrote locally is comprehensive and largely correct against the answer key: 12-component alphabetical IDENTITY_COMPONENT_KEYS (line 5896), 4-key IDENTITY_BACKEND_PARAM_KEYS frozenset excluding api_key/max_retries/request_timeout (line 5911), response_format serialised via json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')) with 'text' fallback (line 6163), run_id keyword-only on compute_run_identity/_run_identity with the two refusal branches and refusal-before-mkdir ordering (lines 6232-6239, 8097-8102), and CURATOR_RUN_ID/uuid4().hex default-minting threaded from __call__ (raw command at index 264 of the full rollout JSON, not visible as rendered text in the transcript's terminal-screen dump).

One instructive example of correct reasoning under pressure: while fixing an existing integration test late in the run, the agent noticed test_cache_with_changed_parse assumed parse_func changes don't fork the cache, cross-checked that against the g4.r1.l-parse-func/say22 chat record, concluded parse_func_hash IS one of the 12 components (matching the hidden requirement), and updated the pre-existing test rather than omitting parse_func_hash to keep the old test green (lines 11105-11206).

The agent's own p5.py patch (visible only in the full rollout JSON's tool_calls, message index 264 -- not in the rendered transcript text) shows __call__'s run_id parameter was added without a preceding bare '*' separator, so it is not strictly keyword-only as the answer key specifies for all three call sites; moot here since nothing reached the grader, but would be worth flagging in a review of the diff itself.

12 of 48 remarks (25%) were never surfaced despite the full corpus being available locally in /tmp/chat.txt the whole time -- a pure recall gap from keyword choice, not a missing source. Because carriers overlap heavily across remarks, none of the 8 graded facts depended solely on a missed remark; the misses reduced redundancy but not (as best as can be judged from the local diff) correctness.

The proximate failure mode was time/turn management: several 'terminal output has not changed for several turns' watchdog interventions appear in the run's final quarter while the agent repeatedly polled long-running background pytest jobs and did baseline-vs-mine comparisons instead of prioritising a commit+push once the implementation and its own tests were green (~line 8911).
